 November 12, 2026 at 1:11 pm CST Expand Shaw Local file photo – A Harvard couple is accused of fraudulently obtaining more than $300 using the Link card and SNAP benefits of a mentally challenged man they were entrusted to care for. (Shaw Local News Network)
 Buy Photo
 By Amanda Marrazzo 
 A Harvard couple is accused of fraudulently obtaining more than $300 using the Link card and SNAP benefits of a man with mental disabilities they were entrusted to care for.
 Christine Sobers, 55, and Brian Sobers, 57, each are charged with aggravated identity theft of $300 to $10,000 of a disabled person, a Class 2 felony. They’re also charged with financially exploiting a disabled person between $300 to $5,000, and unauthorized use of between $150 to $1,000 in food stamps, according to criminal complaints filed in McHenry County court. 
 While in a “position of trust and confidence,” between March 7 and March 19, the couple allegedly used a disabled man’s “SNAP benefits without authorization” as well as his “Illinois LINK card and associated PIN,” according to the complaint. Records allege the couple accessed the man’s SNAP benefits account and obtained $307.76 for his own benefit. 
 A notice of arrest filed by the McHenry County Sheriff’s Office indicates the couple was arrested Wednesday evening, although their mugshots did not yet appear in the jail app Thursday morning.
 On March 2, the day before the alleged fraudulent use of the Link and SNAP benefits, Christine Sobers pressed charges of misdemeanor domestic battery, against the man named as the victim in the couple’s case. Sobers accused him of pushing her down, “causing her to fall to the ground and sustain an injury to her right wrist,” according to the complaint.
 In July, the man was found unfit and not expected to regain fitness and the case was dismissed. Court records signed by Judge Justin Hansen show the man was found “not not guilty.”
 Brian Sobers has a criminal history dating back to 1995, including burglary, theft and being in a park as a sex offender, McHenry County court records show.
 This is a developing story.
